create_row.description: Add a new row to a Baserow table.
create_row.name: create_row

parameters.description: The ID of your Baserow table. Open the table in Baserow and copy the number that appears right after `/table/` in the page's web address.
parameters.name: table_id

parameters.description: The values for the new row, given as column-name and value pairs (for example, Name: 'Acme Inc.', Status: 'Active').
parameters.name: fields

parameters.description: Leave on to use your table's column names (like 'Name' or 'Status'). Turn off to use Baserow's internal field codes (like 'field_123') instead.
parameters.name: user_field_names

id.description: The ID of the newly created row (use it as the Row ID in other actions).

delete_row.description: Permanently remove a row from a Baserow table.
delete_row.name: delete_row

parameters.description: The ID of your Baserow table. Open the table in Baserow and copy the number that appears right after `/table/` in the page's web address.
parameters.name: table_id

parameters.description: The ID of the row to delete. You can find it with the List rows action.
parameters.name: row_id

get_row.description: Get a single row from a Baserow table by its row ID.
get_row.name: get_row

parameters.description: The ID of your Baserow table. Open the table in Baserow and copy the number that appears right after `/table/` in the page's web address.
parameters.name: table_id

parameters.description: The ID of the row to get. You can find it with the List rows action or from a Create row result.
parameters.name: row_id

parameters.description: Leave on to use your table's column names (like 'Name' or 'Status'). Turn off to use Baserow's internal field codes (like 'field_123') instead.
parameters.name: user_field_names

list_rows.description: Get the rows from one of your Baserow tables.
list_rows.name: list_rows

parameters.description: The ID of your Baserow table. Open the table in Baserow and copy the number that appears right after `/table/` in the page's web address.
parameters.name: table_id

parameters.description: The most rows to return, up to 200. Leave blank to return the first page of rows.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Leave on to use your table's column names (like 'Name' or 'Status'). Turn off to use Baserow's internal field codes (like 'field_123') instead.
parameters.name: user_field_names

count.description: Total number of rows in the table.

results.description: The rows on this page. Each row includes its 'id' and its column values.

update_row.description: Change the values of an existing row in a Baserow table.
update_row.name: update_row

parameters.description: The ID of your Baserow table. Open the table in Baserow and copy the number that appears right after `/table/` in the page's web address.
parameters.name: table_id

parameters.description: The ID of the row to update. You can find it with the List rows action or from a Create row result.
parameters.name: row_id

parameters.description: The columns to change and their new values, given as column-name and value pairs (for example, Status: 'Closed'). Columns you leave out keep their current values.
parameters.name: fields

parameters.description: Leave on to use your table's column names (like 'Name' or 'Status'). Turn off to use Baserow's internal field codes (like 'field_123') instead.
parameters.name: user_field_names

description: Create, read, update, and delete rows in your Baserow tables.
